sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Two related but distinct surfaces:

- **Realtime** — WebSocket, SSE, polling; pick by direction + scale.
- **Uploads** — chunked, resumable, progress-aware; signed URLs to S3/GCS.

**Direct-to-storage** uploads (signed URL) keep your app server out of the byte path.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Websockets basics** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Stomp and sockjs** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Server sent events** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Long polling and fallbacks** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **File upload multipart** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Chunked and resumable uploads** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **File download and streaming** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **WebSocket vs SSE** — WS for bidirectional, SSE for server→client only (cheaper).
- **Heartbeats** — proxies kill idle TCP; 30 s pings keep them alive.
- **Resumable uploads** — `tus` protocol or multipart S3.
- **CORS for uploads** — preflight + signed URL signature includes content-type.
- **Backpressure** — slow consumer mustn't crash producer.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For realtime I'd pick SSE for one-way (notifications) and WebSocket for chat. Uploads go direct to object storage via signed URL, chunked + resumable for large files, with progress events surfaced to the UI."*
